title: Civil unrest
label: PUBLIC SAFETY
deck: Move away from active violence and keep your route decisions grounded in current information.
tldr: If violence or dangerous crowd movement is near you, leave the immediate area by a safe route or shelter in a secure place if travel is unsafe. Check local alerts, road closures, and transit changes. Avoid confrontation and keep a way to contact the people you need to reach.
steps: Separate the event from your location
Check what is happening on your route, not just citywide headlines. Peaceful assembly and a nearby dangerous incident are different conditions.
Move away from active violence and blocked roads. If there is no safe exit, shelter inside, away from windows, and update a trusted contact.
Use official local notices for curfews, transport changes, and emergency services, and verify unconfirmed social posts before acting.
Arrange a meeting point and a backup contact if mobile networks are strained. Wait for reliable updates before returning to a disrupted area.
next: Before going out, check whether your route crosses a closure and identify an alternative. Carry basic identification, necessary medication, and phone power.
watch: Do not assume a protest is violent or that a citywide alert applies equally to every neighborhood. If an order applies, read its location, hours, and exceptions.
